findings.evidence: grep: Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/FractionRing.lean:459-465 `ringEquivOfRingEquivHom ... map_one' := ringEquivOfRingEquiv_refl; map_mul' f g := ringEquivOfRingEquiv_comp K K K g f`; PR lines 39-66 supply the identical refl/trans inputs for `ClassGroup.mulEquiv`.
findings.fix: Add `noncomputable def ClassGroup.mulEquivHom : (R ≃+* R) →* MulAut (ClassGroup R) := { toFun := ClassGroup.mulEquiv, map_one' := mulEquiv_refl, map_mul' := fun f g => mulEquiv_trans g f }` (with the `@[simp]` apply lemma), and keep `mulEquiv_involutive` as a corollary of it.
findings.issue: `mulEquiv_involutive` is a special case of the functorial package the PR already has the ingredients for. Mathlib's precedent in the very API family this file mirrors bundles at this point: `IsFractionRing.ringEquivOfRingEquivHom : (A ≃+* A) →* (K ≃+* K)` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/FractionRing.lean:459), built from `ringEquivOfRingEquiv_refl` and `_comp` — the exact analogues of `mulEquiv_refl`/`mulEquiv_trans` here. Without the bundled form the roadmap's stated target ("the nontrivial automorphism acts on Cl(K)") has no group-action/hom to transport along; each downstream use must rebuild it.

summary: Assumptions match Mathlib's `ClassGroup.mulEquiv` exactly and special cases are derived rather than duplicated. But the PR stops one step short of the natural bundled level: having proved refl and trans, the monoid hom `(R ≃+* R) →* MulAut (ClassGroup R)` — the object the roadmap's Galois action actually needs — is left unstated, and `mulEquiv_involutive` is an unbundled shadow of it.
